speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your appointment. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; can you tell me how long you've had this issue and when it first appeared?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum. The patient's history of Crohn's disease, recent corticosteroid use, and the rapid progression of a painful, ulcerative lesion following minor trauma (ant bite) are classic features of this condition. The negative wound culture and lack of systemic infection signs further support this over a bacterial etiology.
